text_note.zh: 这里用通行的简体写法：原始资料的“支子”写作“栀子”，“疎粝”写作“疏粝”，“蹋”写作“踏”。“支子”是栀子的古写法，“蹋”和“踏”意思相同。
text_note.en: This uses the usual simplified forms. The source writes the gardenia with an old form of its name, uses an old form of the character for "coarse", and an older character for "step". The meaning is the same.

readings.zh: 荦确读 luò què，形容山石又大又不平。
readings.en: Read luò què, meaning big, rough rocks.
Read dāng here, meaning facing or right in.

readings.zh: 为人鞿：被别人束缚，“为”表示“被”，读 wéi。
readings.en: Here it means "by" (held back by others), read wéi.

glosses.zh: 荦确：山石又大又多，高低不平。
glosses.en: luò què: big rocks, rough and uneven.

glosses.zh: 行径微：走的小路很窄。微，细小。
glosses.en: xíng jìng wēi: the path is narrow. Wēi means small, thin.

glosses.zh: 升堂：走上佛寺的殿堂。
glosses.en: shēng táng: to go up into the temple hall.

glosses.zh: 新雨足：刚下过一场透雨，雨水很充足。
glosses.en: xīn yǔ zú: a good soaking rain has just fallen.

glosses.zh: 芭蕉：一种叶子又宽又大的植物。
glosses.en: bā jiāo: a plant with very large, wide leaves, like a banana plant.

glosses.zh: 栀子肥：栀子花开得又大又饱满。栀子，一种开白花、很香的灌木。
glosses.en: zhī zǐ féi: the gardenias are full and plump. Gardenia is a bush with sweet white flowers.

glosses.zh: 古壁佛画：古老墙壁上画的佛像。
glosses.en: gǔ bì fó huà: pictures of the Buddha painted on the old walls.

glosses.zh: 所见稀：看到的很模糊，看不太清。一说是很少见的好画。
glosses.en: suǒ jiàn xī: what he could see was faint and unclear. One view: they were rare, fine paintings.

glosses.zh: 拂席：掸掉席子上的灰尘。
glosses.en: fú xí: to brush the dust off the sleeping mat.

glosses.zh: 置羹饭：摆上汤和饭。羹，汤。
glosses.en: zhì gēng fàn: to set out soup and rice. Gēng means soup.

glosses.zh: 疏粝：粗糙的饭菜。
glosses.en: shū lì: plain, coarse food.

glosses.zh: 百虫绝：各种虫子的叫声都停了。
glosses.en: bǎi chóng jué: all the insects have gone quiet.

glosses.zh: 扉：门。
glosses.en: fēi: door.

glosses.zh: 无道路：天刚亮，有雾，看不清路，只能随意走。
glosses.en: wú dào lù: no road to be seen; at dawn the mist hides the way.

glosses.zh: 穷烟霏：走遍了云雾。穷，走到尽头；烟霏，山里的云雾。
glosses.en: qióng yān fēi: walking all through the mist. Qióng means to go to the end of; yān fēi is mountain mist.

glosses.zh: 涧：山间的小溪。
glosses.en: jiàn: a mountain stream.

glosses.zh: 纷烂漫：颜色繁多，鲜艳夺目。
glosses.en: fēn làn màn: many bright colors, everywhere.

glosses.zh: 松枥：松树和栎树。枥，就是栎树。
glosses.en: sōng lì: pines and oaks.

glosses.zh: 十围：十个人手拉手才抱得过来，形容树非常粗。
glosses.en: shí wéi: ten armspans around, so thick that ten people holding hands could just circle it.

glosses.zh: 当流：对着水流，站在溪水中。
glosses.en: dāng liú: standing right in the flowing water.

glosses.zh: 赤足：光着脚。
glosses.en: chì zú: barefoot.

glosses.zh: 激激：水流冲击石头的声音。
glosses.en: jī jī: the sound of water dashing on rocks.

glosses.zh: 局束：拘束，受限制，放不开手脚。
glosses.en: jú shù: cramped, held in, not free.

glosses.zh: 为人鞿：被人管着，像马被缰绳套住一样。鞿，马的缰绳。
glosses.en: wéi rén jī: to be held by others, like a horse in a bridle. Jī is a bridle.

glosses.zh: 嗟哉：唉，感叹的声音。
glosses.en: jiē zāi: ah! a sigh.

glosses.zh: 吾党二三子：我的这几个朋友。吾党，跟我志同道合的人。
glosses.en: wú dǎng èr sān zǐ: my few friends, the people who think as I do.

glosses.zh: 安得：怎么能。
glosses.en: ān dé: how can we?

glosses.zh: 不更归：不再回去。一说意思是怎么能到老都不回到这里来。
glosses.en: bù gèng guī: not go back again (to the world of office). Another reading: how could we grow old without coming back here?

translation.zh: 山石又大又多，高低不平，山路窄窄的。
translation.en: The mountain rocks are big and rough; the path is thin.

translation.zh: 黄昏时我来到寺庙，蝙蝠在空中飞。
translation.en: At dusk I reach the temple, and bats are flying.

translation.zh: 走上殿堂，坐在台阶上，刚下过一场透雨，
translation.en: I go up to the hall and sit on the steps. A good rain has just fallen.

translation.zh: 芭蕉叶子又宽又大，栀子花开得饱满。
translation.en: The banana leaves are broad, and the gardenias are full.

translation.zh: 和尚说古墙上的佛像画得很好，
translation.en: A monk says the Buddha paintings on the old walls are fine.

translation.zh: 他拿火来照，我看到的却模模糊糊。
translation.en: He brings a light to show me, but I can see only a little.

translation.zh: 他为我铺床、掸席子，摆上汤和饭，
translation.en: He makes my bed, brushes the mat, and sets out soup and rice.

translation.zh: 饭菜虽然粗糙，也足够让我吃饱。
translation.en: The food is plain, but enough to fill me.

translation.zh: 夜深了，我静静躺着，虫声都停了，
translation.en: Deep in the night I lie still; the insects have all gone quiet.

translation.zh: 清亮的月亮从山岭上升起，月光照进门里。
translation.en: A clear moon rises over the ridge and shines through the door.

translation.zh: 天亮后我一个人离开，看不清道路，
translation.en: At dawn I leave alone, and there is no path to be seen.

translation.zh: 高高低低，进进出出，走遍了云雾。
translation.en: Up and down, in and out, I walk through all the mist.

translation.zh: 山花红，溪水绿，到处颜色鲜艳，
translation.en: Red hills, green streams, bright colors everywhere.

translation.zh: 不时看到松树和栎树，都有十人合抱那么粗。
translation.en: Now and then I see pines and oaks, ten armspans thick.

translation.zh: 站在溪流里，光着脚踩着溪中的石头，
translation.en: I stand in the stream and step barefoot on its stones.

translation.zh: 水声哗哗，风吹动我的衣服。
translation.en: The water roars, and the wind blows my clothes.

translation.zh: 人生能这样，自然是快乐的，
translation.en: A life like this is happy in itself.

translation.zh: 何必拘拘束束，被别人管着呢？
translation.en: Why must we be cramped, held by others like a horse in a bridle?

translation.zh: 唉，我那几个志同道合的朋友啊，
translation.en: Ah, my few like-minded friends,

translation.zh: 怎么能到老都不再回去做官呢！
translation.en: how can we grow old and never go back again?

background.zh: 一般认为，这首诗写于唐德宗贞元十七年（801年）。当时韩愈离开徐州，住在洛阳。他和几个朋友一起游洛阳北面的惠林寺，傍晚到寺里住了一夜，第二天早上离开。诗按时间顺序写下了这次游玩。题目“山石”取自第一句开头两个字，是古诗常用的取题方法。
background.en: The poem is usually dated to 801. Han Yu had left Xuzhou and was living in Luoyang. With a few friends he visited Huilin Temple, north of Luoyang. They arrived at dusk, stayed the night and left the next morning. The poem follows the trip in order of time. The title, "Mountain Rocks", is just the first two characters of the first line, an old way of naming poems.

author_note.zh: 韩愈（768—824），唐代文学家，“唐宋八大家”之首，主张写文章要像古人那样朴实有内容。他的诗也很有特点，常常用写文章的方法写诗，直接、有力。这首诗像一篇游记，一步一步写下所见所感。
author_note.en: Han Yu (768–824) was a Tang writer, first of the Eight Great Prose Masters of Tang and Song. He wanted writing to be plain and full of substance, like the ancients. His poems are bold and direct, often written the way one writes prose. This poem reads like a travel diary, step by step.

appreciation.zh: 这首诗像一部小电影，镜头跟着诗人走。黄昏，山路窄，蝙蝠飞；雨后的寺院里，芭蕉叶大，栀子花肥。和尚举着火光照壁画，又铺床端饭。夜里虫声停了，月光照进门来，非常安静。第二天早上，雾里找不到路，诗人高高低低地走，忽然眼前一亮：红的山，绿的水，粗大的老树。他光脚站在溪水里，听水声，任风吹衣，多自在！最后他说出心里话：人生这样就很快乐，何必被官场管着呢？从黄昏到夜里到清晨，景物一层层展开，心情也越来越开朗。
appreciation.en: This poem is like a short film, with the camera following the poet. At dusk the path is narrow and bats are flying. In the temple after rain, the banana leaves are big and the gardenias full. A monk holds up a light to the wall paintings, then makes the bed and brings food. At night the insects stop and moonlight comes through the door. All is very still. Next morning he cannot find the path in the mist. He walks up and down, and then the view opens: red hills, green water, huge old trees. He stands barefoot in the stream, listening to the water, letting the wind blow his clothes. How free he feels! At the end he says what is in his heart: a life like this is happy enough, so why be held in by official life? From dusk to night to morning, the scenes unfold one by one, and his mood grows brighter and brighter.
